## Findings and required review
- Data-quality factors needed a named, evidence-based practice task: added to weeks 13–14 review.
- Earlier diagram work centred on four tables: added an original six-table interpretation extension and fresh four-table creation task. Teachers must visually compare crow's-foot conventions with the support booklet and review student diagrams.
- The conceptual dictionary describes rules (label lengths, identifier format, CategoryName uniqueness, default return status) that the SQLite starter does not all enforce. The review requires an explicit intended/implemented comparison. The starter remains a scaffold; it does not claim full enforcement, calendar-date validation or overlapping-loan prevention.
- Security types are mapped, but a dense table is not classroom mastery evidence. Use retrieval/transfer scenarios and independent explanations.
- Privacy context is dated. Recheck current federal/WA law and school procedures before operational reuse.
- Practical creation, independent modelling, query/constraint tests, recovery, classroom pacing, accessibility and independent teacher review still need learner evidence. The paper samples content; it cannot assess the whole practical course.

## Weeks 13–16
13–14 integrated review: eight lessons including data-quality/model/schema repair, security transfer, controlled theory practice and feedback.
15 consolidation: four lessons for diagnosis, stations, transfer and revision planning.
16 exam preparation: four lessons for two practice halves, explained feedback and targeted repair.
17–18 blocked exams: no new teaching or project deadlines. With weeks 1–12 this remains 64 teaching lessons; the 14 project lessons are already embedded.
